hints: At constant speed on a level road, the driving force equals the resistance force: $F = 3000\text{ N}$.
walkthrough:
On a horizontal road at constant speed, the driving force balances the resistance:
$$F = 3000\text{ N}$$

Calculate the required engine power:
$$P = F \times v = 3000 \times 30 = 90000\text{ W} = 90\text{ kW}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the force balance for motion at constant speed on horizontal ground ($a = 0$):
$$\Sigma F = 0 \implies F_D - R = 0 \implies F_D = R = 3000\text{ N}$$

State the formula relating power to driving force and speed:
$$P = F_D \times v$$
Substitute $F_D = 3000\text{ N}$ and $v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 3000 \times 30 = 90000\text{ W} = 90\text{ kW}$$

hints: Calculate the loss in kinetic energy as the speed drops from $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}m(30^2 - 25^2)$.
Express the distance up the slope in terms of the vertical height $h$: $d = \frac{h}{\sin 2^\circ}$.
Formulate the energy balance: $\Delta E_k = mgh + R\left(\frac{h}{\sin 2^\circ}\right)$.
Factor out $h$ and solve for the vertical height.
walkthrough:
Calculate the kinetic energy lost by the lorry between $A$ and $B$:
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}m\left(u^2 - v^2\right) = \frac{1}{2}(25000)\left(30^2 - 25^2\right) = 12500(900 - 625) = 12500(275) = 3437500\text{ J}$$

Express the distance travelled along the $2^\circ$ incline in terms of the height $h$:
$$d = \frac{h}{\sin 2^\circ}$$
Then the work done against the $3000\text{ N}$ resistance force is:
$$W_{\text{res}} = R d = \frac{3000h}{\sin 2^\circ}$$

Apply the work-energy theorem for the unpowered ascent:
$$\Delta E_k = \text{Gain in PE} + W_{\text{res}}$$
$$3437500 = 25000(10)h + \frac{3000h}{\sin 2^\circ}$$
$$3437500 = 250000h + 85961.1h = 335961.1h$$

Solve for the vertical height $h$:
$$h = \frac{3437500}{335961.1} \approx 10.232\text{ m} \approx 10.2\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the conservation of energy principle with non-conservative resistance forces:
$$\text{Loss in KE} = \text{Gain in PE} + W_{\text{res}}$$
$$\frac{1}{2}m u^2 - \frac{1}{2}m v^2 = mgh + R d$$

Calculate the change in kinetic energy ($m = 25000\text{ kg}$, $u = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$):
$$\text{Loss in KE} = \frac{1}{2} \times 25000 \times (30^2 - 25^2) = 12500 \times (900 - 625)$$
$$12500 \times 275 = 3437500\text{ J}$$

Relate distance $d$ along the $2^\circ$ incline to the vertical rise $h$:
$$h = d\sin 2^\circ \implies d = \frac{h}{\sin 2^\circ}$$
Express the work done against resistance:
$$W_{\text{res}} = 3000d = \frac{3000h}{\sin 2^\circ}$$
Evaluate the coefficient with $\sin 2^\circ \approx 0.0348995$:
$$\frac{3000}{\sin 2^\circ} \approx \frac{3000}{0.0348995} \approx 85961.12$$

Express the gain in gravitational potential energy:
$$\text{Gain in PE} = mgh = 25000 \times 10 \times h = 250000h$$

Equate the energy terms and solve for $h$:
$$3437500 = 250000h + 85961.12h = 335961.12h$$
$$h = \frac{3437500}{335961.12} \approx 10.2318\text{ m}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $h = 10.2\text{ m}$.

ai_rubric.Applying the Work\u2013Energy Principle: Sets up $3437500 = 250000h + \frac{3000h}{\sin 2^\circ}$ and solves for $h = 10.2\text{ m}$.
